policy_rows.selected: {"consequence":"A brief local conversation gathers estimates from people who might overlook an online form and combines them for preparation.","decision":"How should organizers learn what neighbors expect to contribute?","mechanism":"Block volunteers ask interested neighbors about expected contributions and send category summaries to the organizers."}

{"consequence":"People organize their own visits within visible capacity, giving volunteers a rough forecast of when incoming contributions will arrive.","decision":"How should contribution arrivals be spread across the intake period?","mechanism":"Contributors choose available arrival windows on the intake sheet before bringing their household goods."}

{"consequence":"Questions about damage or missing parts can be answered immediately before an item is accepted for display.","decision":"How should contributed goods be checked before display?","mechanism":"Intake volunteers inspect each contribution with the condition checklist while its contributor is present."}

{"consequence":"The same person translates the conversation into the standard fields, reducing differences in how descriptions and known limitations are presented.","decision":"How should useful item descriptions be prepared?","mechanism":"Intake volunteers ask contributors for item details and write the labels during acceptance."}

{"consequence":"Visitors looking for kitchen, bedroom, or living-room items can begin with a familiar part of the home.","decision":"How should the display tables be organized?","mechanism":"Volunteers group household goods by their ordinary room of use and label the display tables accordingly."}

{"consequence":"One repeating circuit keeps stock moving without requiring table volunteers to leave their visitors or send individual requests.","decision":"How should reserve stock reach the display tables?","mechanism":"A runner checks the display tables at regular intervals and brings reserve goods that fit the available spaces."}

{"consequence":"A common explanation reaches several visitors together while personal questions can be handled after the group moves on.","decision":"How should arriving visitors learn how the fair works?","mechanism":"A welcome volunteer gives short introductions to small arriving groups and then offers individual clarification beside the entrance diagram."}

{"consequence":"The visible request times determine priority, so people can understand the result without a separate comparison of their reasons for wanting it.","decision":"How should competing requests for the same item be settled?","mechanism":"A volunteer awards the item to the earliest recorded requester when its decision window closes."}

{"consequence":"A single handover establishes responsibility and makes the promised collection time clear to both people.","decision":"How should claimed items be held while recipients continue browsing?","mechanism":"Recipients bring claimed items to the holding volunteer, who records their names and deadlines before placing the goods on shelves."}

{"consequence":"Visitors handle a single bundle, reducing the chance that pieces from one contribution become separated during browsing.","decision":"How should pieces of a complete set remain together?","mechanism":"Volunteers bag or tie each complete set together before it reaches the display table, leaving its description visible."}

{"consequence":"Assistance follows goods that are ready to leave, keeping the handover simple at the point where carrying begins.","decision":"How should visitors arrange help carrying goods out?","mechanism":"Visitors request carrying help at collection, and a volunteer assigns the next available helper and cart."}

{"consequence":"People can prepare for specific duties, and the coordinator can see uncovered work before the event begins.","decision":"How should volunteers receive their working assignments?","mechanism":"The coordinator assigns volunteer shifts from the availability and preference list and circulates the resulting roster before the fair."}

{"consequence":"Requests are seen where suitable goods are most likely to arrive, while the collection point gathers the resulting match notices.","decision":"How should requests for currently missing goods be recorded?","mechanism":"Visitors place wanted-item notes beside the relevant category signs, and table volunteers move matched notes to a collection point."}

{"consequence":"The written update happens before the exit handover, separating record work from the movement of items.","decision":"How should outgoing goods be recorded at collection?","mechanism":"Recipients present their claim records to a recording volunteer, then show a checked collection slip when taking the goods out."}

{"consequence":"Returned goods are easy to find, and the donation pile is already separated for the later arranged pickup.","decision":"How should unclaimed goods be processed after the fair closes?","mechanism":"Volunteers sort all unclaimed goods by recorded return or donation preference before contributors enter the closing collection period."}

{"consequence":"Each group can explain problems in its own terms before organizers identify changes that would help more than one role.","decision":"How should organizers learn which parts of the fair need improvement?","mechanism":"Organizers hold brief separate conversations with visitors, contributors, and volunteers, then compare notes about the fair’s main routines."}
